We are asked to participate in a cross-examination discussion, reviewing all experts' verdicts. The original verdict was bearish with 75% confidence. Now we must reconsider given the other experts' views. We are simulating Nassim Taleb's perspective: focus on fragility, asymmetry, tail risks, antifragility, skin in the game, optionality. The other experts are mostly neutral or cautiously bullish, with some acknowledging overbought conditions but not fully bearish. Notable: Druckenmiller is bullish tilt 70%, Dalio bullish, Soros sees reflexive boom, Howard Marks sees late-cycle, Tepper is bearish with stagflation risk. We need to see if we should revise. According to Taleb, the key is hidden fragility and asymmetry. The core fragility: 61% TSMC, overbought, high PE, premium. The AI narrative is all-encompassing; any black swan could cause >50% loss. No optionality, just linear exposure. So bearish remains justified. But maybe we need to consider if Taleb would see something like "antifragility" from volatility? No. The ETF is purely long beta, fragile. Tail risks: geopolitical, Taiwan strait, AI bust. The positive macro data only makes it more fragile if it's already priced in. So my confidence might stay high, maybe even increase, given many experts are optimistic yet the setup is fragile. I'll maintain bearish, perhaps confidence 80% due to the consensus optimism (a contrarian indicator). In the analysis process, I'll note that other experts acknowledge overbought but downplay fragility, which is a sign of complacency—increasing the fragility. So I'll keep my verdict.

Final JSON: bearish, 80, reasoning with fragility, asymmetry, tail risks, no optionality.
